name: minijinja_render
description: Render a MiniJinja template without a JSON context. The template is the only positional argument — to supply variables, including columns or json_object built from columns, use minijinja_render_with_context. Options are keyword-only named parameters (`name := value`) with defaults; they must be constant expressions, unknown option names or values of the wrong type are rejected when the query is bound, and an explicit NULL option makes the result NULL.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: Template source (or a template name when `template_path` is set).

parameters.name: autoescape
parameters.description: HTML-escape interpolated values (`B&O` becomes `B&O`). Pass `false` for plain text, configs, SQL or JSON output.

parameters.name: template_path
parameters.description: Directory (or a file, whose directory is used) to load templates from. When set, `template` is the name of a template file there, which enables `{% include %}` / `{% extends %}`. Empty means inline templates only.

parameters.name: undefined_behavior
parameters.description: How undefined variables are treated: `'lenient'` renders a missing variable as empty but errors on attribute access through it, `'chainable'` also renders attribute access on undefined values as empty, `'semi_strict'` and `'strict'` raise errors. Any other value is a binder error.

parameters.name: autoescape_extensions
parameters.description: When non-empty, HTML autoescape applies only to templates whose name ends with one of these suffixes (for example `['.html']`), overriding `autoescape` — useful with `template_path`. Must not contain NULL elements.

name: minijinja_render_with_context
description: Render a MiniJinja template with a JSON context, including contexts built from columns with json_object. Supports variables, filters, conditionals, for loops and autoescaping. Options are keyword-only named parameters (`name := value`) with defaults; they must be constant expressions, unknown option names or values of the wrong type are rejected when the query is bound, and an explicit NULL option makes the result NULL.

examples.code: SELECT minijinja_render_with_context('{% for x in xs %}{{ x }}{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}{% endfor %}', '{"xs":["A","B","C"]}');

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: Template source (or a template name when `template_path` is set).

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: JSON context the template is rendered against — a literal, a JSON column, or `json_object(...)` built from columns.

parameters.name: autoescape
parameters.description: HTML-escape interpolated values (`B&O` becomes `B&O`). Pass `false` for plain text, configs, SQL or JSON output.

parameters.name: template_path
parameters.description: Directory (or a file, whose directory is used) to load templates from. When set, `template` is the name of a template file there, which enables `{% include %}` / `{% extends %}`. Empty means inline templates only.

parameters.name: undefined_behavior
parameters.description: How undefined variables are treated: `'lenient'` renders a missing variable as empty but errors on attribute access through it, `'chainable'` also renders attribute access on undefined values as empty, `'semi_strict'` and `'strict'` raise errors. Any other value is a binder error.

parameters.name: autoescape_extensions
parameters.description: When non-empty, HTML autoescape applies only to templates whose name ends with one of these suffixes (for example `['.html']`), overriding `autoescape` — useful with `template_path`. Must not contain NULL elements.
